column1: # Known Layer-3 failures: comparisons that breach the blocking threshold because
# of a filed, open defect in ltl — not because the harness is miscalibrated.
# An entry suppresses the block for exactly one (scenario, file_kind, column,
# key_class) combination and is reported as XFAIL, with its issue, on every run.
# It is NOT a tolerance: the comparison still happens and the deviation is still
# printed.
# Entries are self-clearing. If a registered comparison PASSES, the engine fails
# the run with "known failure no longer reproduces" — so the fix cannot land
# without the entry being removed in the same change.
# Columns:
#   scenario    — scenario id from scenarios.tsv
#   file_kind   — messages | stats
#   column      — the CSV column whose comparison is expected to breach
#   key_class   — merged (row key contains the consolidation wildcard '*')
#                 | any
#   issue       — the open defect this is waiting on
#   note        — why, in one line
# #460: bin-model percentiles are computed from a re-projected representation,
# and the accuracy bound written for them describes a histogram that has never
# been re-projected.
# A consolidated row's percentiles are derived from the member histograms of the
# keys the row absorbed, projected onto one shared geometry. The oracle derives
# the same row by pooling those keys' raw durations into a single histogram. One
# projection is not zero projections, so the two cannot agree closer than one
# bucket - 4.44% at the per-message surface's default 53 buckets per decade.
# Every entry below is inside that bound; IQR entries are larger because an IQR
# is a difference of two percentiles and carries both.
# These were registered against #459 (combination order) on 2026-08-26 on the
# assumption that its compounding was the cause. It was not: #459 landed on
# 2026-08-27, removing the compounding and proving order-independence, and these
# comparisons still breach - because they are the accuracy bound, which #460
# owns and is correcting. Measured on real grouped rows, a single projection
# leaves the one-bucket bound on 1.54% (tomcat) and 2.08% (thingworx) of
# evaluations; see features/459-bin-counter-combination-order.md sections 7 and 9.
# They clear when #460 either corrects the bound (in which case the harness
# threshold for merged bin rows follows it) or removes the projection. The
# entries are self-clearing and the engine will insist.
